coordinates.note: Approximate, campus-grade: the centre of the OpenStreetMap way of the Vue-des-Alpes road tunnel (about 2.5 km across); the laboratory lies somewhere in that tunnel. No paper or official page read gives a latitude and longitude for the laboratory ('near Neuchâtel (Switzerland)'), so this point is not the laboratory's position.

depth_mwe.quote: The depth of 620 m.w.e. (235 m of rock overburden) of the laboratory in the Vue-des-Alpes tunnel reduces the muon flux

name: Vue-des-Alpes underground laboratory (tunnel site)
notes: The DELight TAUP 2025 paper quotes 230 m of rock and ~630 mwe for the same laboratory; the GeMSE papers (the laboratory's own users) give 235 m and 620 m.w.e., which are recorded.

summary.plain: A small underground space inside the Vue-des-Alpes road tunnel in the Swiss Jura mountains, about 235 metres below the surface.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory in the Vue-des-Alpes tunnel near Neuchâtel: 235 m rock overburden, 620 m.w.e., muon flux 8.3e-2 m^-2 s^-1; electricity and network only.
